title: Copenhagen Atomics and Urenco partner on planned deconversion facility
summary: Copenhagen Atomics and Urenco have signed a memorandum of understanding to develop a deconversion plant that would produce uranium tetrafluoride (UF4) at a Copenhagen Atomics facility. The MOU establishes a new framework for cooperation between a developer primarily exploring molten salt reactors (MSRs) and a global supplier of uranium enrichment services. Copenhagen Atomics—the MSR developer—seeks to employ Urenco’s expertise in producing uranium hexafluoride (UF6) to establish a UF6-to-UF4 pathway. This would provide Copenhagen Atomics with the UF4 feedstock its MSRs require. The company also has purchased low-enriched uranium from Urenco as part of their collaboration.

title: Canada assesses its space reactor capabilities
summary: The Canadian Space Agency announced a request for information (RFI) seeking input from Canadian industry and academia on the country’s technologies and capabilities related to lunar microreactors, aiming to identify areas where Canada has differentiated or strategically valuable capabilities. The agency identifies fission power as complementary to solar power and batteries for lunar missions, including for exploration, mobility, and future crewed operations. The RFI aims to assess technologies that are at a technology readiness level of at least 2, which could be for a reactor or specific subsystems.

title: INL and Purdue University collaborate on construction demonstration
summary: A newly announced collaboration between Idaho National Laboratory’s National Reactor Innovation Center (NRIC) and Purdue University’s Applied Research Institute (PARI) will focus on demonstrating construction techniques for reducing costs and risks of new reactors. The project, which also includes the Electric Power Research Institute and the Nuclear Energy Institute, is part of the implementation of NRIC’s Advanced Construction Technology Initiative (ACTI).

title: China Pours First Concrete For HTGR At ‘World’s First’ Hybrid Nuclear Power Station
summary: The first batch of concrete has been poured for the nuclear island of the high-temperature gas-cooled reactor (HTGR) that forms part the first phase of a hybrid nuclear power station in Jiangsu province, eastern China. The facility, known as the Jiangsu Xuwei Nuclear Heating and Power Plant, will supply both industrial heat and electricity by coupling the Chilong One HTGR with two Hualong One pressurised water reactors (PWRs). CNNC said first concrete had now been poured for the 600-MW HTGR. That follows the pouring of first concrete in January for the nuclear island of Unit 1, a Hualong One PWR.
